      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "# Task 1: Find Unique Elements from an Array\n",
        "\n",
        "**Difficulty:** Easy\n",
        "\n",
        "## Problem Statement\n",
        "\n",
        "Write a Python program that:\n",
        "\n",
        "1. Takes an array (list) as input from the user.\n",
        "2. Passes the array to a function.\n",
        "3. The function should return all unique elements present in the array.\n",
        "4. Display the unique elements to the user.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Example\n",
        "\n",
        "Input:\n",
        "\n",
        "```python\n",
        "[1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 1, 5]\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "Output:\n",
        "\n",
        "```python\n",
        "[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "## Learning Objectives\n",
        "\n",
        "* Variables\n",
        "* Lists\n",
        "* Loops\n",
        "* Functions\n",
        "* Basic Python Syntax\n",
        "\n",
        "After completing this task, you should be comfortable writing loops and functions in Python, especially if you already have experience with C/C++.\n"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "2C6gYKeJtrr0"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "def unique_elements(a):\n",
        "    mpp = []\n",
        "    for x in a:\n",
        "        if x not in mpp:\n",
        "            mpp.append(x)\n",
        "    return mpp\n",
        "\n",
        "a = list(map(int, input(\"Enter elements separated by spaces: \").split()))\n",
        "\n",
        "print(unique_elements(a))"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "KYHmaLqktsAc",
        "outputId": "8835254a-fa78-427b-869e-67b7f2eee3bb"
      },
      "execution_count": null,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Enter elements separated by spaces: 2 3 1 2 4 5 6 5 5 3 1 2\n",
            "[2, 3, 1, 4, 5, 6]\n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },

        "# **Task 2: Matrix Operations**\n",
        "\n",
        "**Difficulty:** Medium\n",
        "\n",
        "## Problem Statement\n",
        "\n",
        "### Part A: Matrix Transpose\n",
        "\n",
        "Given a matrix, print its transpose.\n",
        "\n",
        "Example:\n",
        "\n",
        "Input:\n",
        "\n",
        "```text\n",
        "1 2 3\n",
        "4 5 6\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "Output:\n",
        "\n",
        "```text\n",
        "1 4\n",
        "2 5\n",
        "3 6\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "### Part B: Diagonal Sums\n",
        "\n",
        "For a square matrix, calculate:\n",
        "\n",
        "* Primary Diagonal Sum\n",
        "* Secondary Diagonal Sum\n",
        "\n",
        "Example:\n",
        "\n",
        "Input:\n",
        "\n",
        "```text\n",
        "1 2 3\n",
        "4 5 6\n",
        "7 8 9\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "Output:\n",
        "\n",
        "```text\n",
        "Primary Diagonal Sum = 15\n",
        "Secondary Diagonal Sum = 15\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "## Learning Objectives\n",
        "\n",
        "* Working with 2D Lists (Matrices)\n",
        "* Nested Loops\n",
        "* Matrix Traversal\n",
        "* Index-Based Operations\n",
        "\n",
        "After completing this task, you will understand how matrices are represented and manipulated in Python."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "PtTTodkWtsU5"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "r=int(input(\"Enter number of rows: \"))\n",
        "c=int(input(\"Enter number of columns: \"))\n",
        "print(\"Enter matrix:\")\n",
        "a = []\n",
        "for i in range(r):\n",
        "    a.append(list(map(int,input().split())))\n",
        "a = np.array(a)\n",
        "print(\"\\nTranspose:\")\n",
        "print(a.T)\n",
        "if r==c:\n",
        "    p=np.trace(a)\n",
        "    s=np.trace(np.fliplr(a))\n",
        "    print(\"\\nPrimary Diagonal Sum: \",p)\n",
        "    print(\"Secondary Diagonal Sum: \",s)\n",
        "else:\n",
        "    print(\"\\nRectangular matrices are not allowed\")"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "Ac-GefRDtsk5",
        "outputId": "3c99d23d-bccd-4d67-8688-83cd680bb9f8"
      },

            "\n",
            "Transpose:\n",
            "[[1 4 7]\n",
            " [2 5 8]\n",
            " [3 6 9]]\n",
            "\n",
            "Primary Diagonal Sum:  15\n",
            "Secondary Diagonal Sum:  15\n"
          ]

        "# Task 3: String Tokenization\n",
        "\n",
        "**Difficulty:** Hard ⭐⭐⭐\n",
        "\n",
        "## Problem Statement\n",
        "\n",
        "Tokenization is one of the most fundamental concepts used in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Large Language Models (LLMs).\n",
        "\n",
        "Your task is to tokenize a given string into individual words.\n",
        "\n",
        "Example:\n",
        "\n",
        "Input:\n",
        "\n",
        "```python\n",
        "\"I am Tirth Patel\"\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "Output:\n",
        "\n",
        "```python\n",
        "[\"I\", \"am\", \"Tirth\", \"Patel\"]\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "### Dataset\n",
        "\n",
        "Use the following code to download the text data:\n",
        "\n",
        "```python\n",
        "import requests\n",
        "\n",
        "url = \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spyguessgame-boop/own_dataset/refs/heads/main/data.txt\"\n",
        "\n",
        "response = requests.get(url)\n",
        "response.raise_for_status()\n",
        "\n",
        "text_data = response.text\n",
        "\n",
        "text_data = text_data[:1000]\n",
        "print(text_data)\n",
        "```\n",
        "\n",
        "Run the code above to obtain the text and then write a Python program that tokenizes the content into words.\n",
        "\n",
        "### Bonus Challenge\n",
        "\n",
        "* Count the total number of tokens.\n",
        "* Find the most frequent token.\n",
        "* Remove punctuation before tokenization.\n",
        "\n",
        "## Learning Objectives\n",
        "\n",
        "* String Manipulation\n",
        "* Text Processing\n",
        "* Lists\n",
        "* Real-World Data Handling\n",
        "* Introduction to NLP and LLM Pipelines\n",
        "\n",
        "Tokenization may appear simple, but it is one of the first and most important steps in how modern LLMs process text."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "dKC9JFQJtsyu"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "import requests\n",
        "\n",
        "url = \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spyguessgame-boop/own_dataset/refs/heads/main/data.txt\"\n",
        "\n",
        "response = requests.get(url)\n",
        "response.raise_for_status()\n",
        "\n",
        "text_data = response.text\n",
        "\n",
        "text_data = text_data[:1000]\n",
        "print(text_data)"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "S8dGWwIwts96",
        "outputId": "36cf520c-d9db-4574-efcb-6674cd91400a"
      },
      "execution_count": null,
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "\n",
            "THE 'BODY OF THE NATION'\n",
            "\n",
            "\n",
            "BUT the basin of the Mississippi is the Body of The Nation. All the other parts are but members, important in themselves, yet more important in their relations to this. Exclusive of the Lake basin and of 300,000 square miles in Texas and New Mexico, which in many aspects form a part of it, this basin contains about 1,250,000 square miles. The valley of the frozen Obi approaches it in extent; that of La Plata comes next in space, and probably in habitable capacity, having about eight-ninths of its area; then comes that of the Yenisei, with about seven-ninths; the Lena, Amoor, Hoang-ho, Yang-tse-kiang, and Nile, five-ninths; the Ganges, less than one-half; the Indus, less than one-third; the Euphrates, one-fifth; the Rhine, one-fifteenth. It exceeds in extent the whole of Europe, exclusive of Russia, Norway, and Sweden. It would contain austria four times, germany \n"
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "import string\n",
        "from collections import Counter\n",
        "text_data = text_data.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))\n",
        "tokens = text_data.split()\n",
        "count = len(tokens)\n",
        "freq = Counter(tokens)\n",
        "most_frequent = freq.most_common(1)[0]\n",
        "print(tokens)\n",
        "print(\"Total Tokens =\", count)\n",
        "print(\"Most Frequent Token =\", most_frequent[0])\n",
        "print(\"Frequency =\", most_frequent[1])"
      ],
      "metadata": {
